summary: SAMPLE: the round 2 rival corners aggressive players, a single sweep beats the CPU, and casual players drift away after round 2.

findings.title: Round 2 is a wall for aggressive players
findings.narrative: Rushers win 60% of round 1 and only 19% of round 2, and most of those losses end pinned against the left wall. 53% of rushers quit from frustration or boredom.

seeds.why: cornered and KO'd at the left wall in round 2

findings.suggestion: Soften the round 2 rival: add a short wall-bounce or push-back so a cornered player can escape.

precedent.title: Corner pressure and wall breaks in fighting game design
precedent.snippet: Sample precedent link: corner escapes keep losing players engaged.

findings.title: Sweep spam wins 95% of rounds
findings.narrative: Cheesers who repeat the low sweep win 95% of their rounds in 26 s on average. The rival never learns to block low.
findings.suggestion: Make SWEEP punishable on block (longer recovery) and let the CPU rival switch to low guard after two sweeps.

precedent.title: Sweep recovery and low-guard adaptation
precedent.snippet: Sample precedent link: long recovery on low attacks is the usual fix.

findings.title: Casual players leave after two rounds
findings.narrative: 93% of casual players stop because of boredom or frustration, most after round 2 or 3. Nothing new appears between rounds.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a new move or arena prop in round 2 to give casual players a reason to stay.

findings.title: Fighter can get stuck in the block state
findings.narrative: 9 rounds report the persona fighter frozen in BLOCK for more than two seconds. It shows up mostly in long turtle rounds (about 82 s).
findings.suggestion: Release guard when the block input is held through a knockdown recovery.
